prompt_text: Who is the best moving company in Pleasanton CA for a local move?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one single “best” mover for everyone — the right company depends on your size of move, budget, timing, and special needs (stairs, piano, disassembly, short‑term storage). That said, here’s a practical way to get the best local mover in Pleasanton plus a few reputable companies to start with.

Quick shortlist to research (all operate in the Bay Area / Tri‑Valley):
- Two Men and a Truck (Tri‑Valley franchise) — widely available, good for standard household moves and hourly/local work.  
- Bellhop — app‑based service with transparent pricing and good tech for scheduling.  
- College HUNKS Hauling Junk & Moving (Bay Area) — good customer service and packing help for smaller moves.  
- Local Tri‑Valley / East Bay movers (look for “Tri‑Valley Movers”, “Pleasanton movers”, or “East Bay movers” on Yelp/Google) — sometimes lower cost and very experienced with neighborhood specifics.

How to pick the best one for your move:
1. Check recent Google and Yelp ratings and read several recent reviews.  
2. Verify they’re licensed: California household goods movers should be registered with the CA Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) — ask for their CPUC or DOT number.  
3. Get at least 3 in‑home (or video) written estimates — ask whether the estimate is binding or not.  
4. Ask about insurance/valuation options (released value vs full value coverage), and what’s included (padding, shrinkwrap, disassembly).  
5. Confirm hourly rates, minimums, extra fees (stairs, long carries, elevator, bulky items) and cancellation policy.  
6. Ask about crew size and how long similar moves in your neighborhood take.

If you tell me:
- approximate date,  
- size of your move (studio/1BR/2BR/3BR), and  
- any special items (piano, gun safe, antiques),  

I can suggest the best 2–3 options to contact and draft questions/messages to send for estimates.
